title: p256-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho with the negation map

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed NIST P-256 generator P, the parallel Pollard rho algorithm of proof.md with the negation map, R=2048 adding walks, look-ahead, distinguished points of 32 trailing zero bits, w=2^40 walks and k=27*2^123 useful steps recovers x with success probability at least 0.509 under the disclosed random-walk and fruitless-cycle heuristics, using at most 2^129.046492 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^103.754888 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^27.288456 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. Actual P-256 arithmetic is charged through justified scalar AArch64 instruction counts divided by C=1000; a P-256 addition is not one unit. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic generic accounting, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check negation-map Pollard rho with look-ahead and distinguished points on a small prime-order Weierstrass curve. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
